title: Continuous integral coefficients agree with their normalized completed presentation
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l a finite extension, A its valuation ring with the valuation topology, and X any scheme [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. Let A_X be the sheaf of continuous A-valued functions, using the lifted section convention [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Let O be the standard valuation subring in E, O^up its universe lift, and B_X the completed coefficient sheaf of its adic datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. There exist a ring equivalence s:A^up≃O^up and a ring-sheaf isomorphism c:B_X≃A_X. They respect the actual scalar maps: the constant sheaf map induced by s followed by the completed scalar map O^up_X→B_X [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] equals the constant-section map A^up_X→A_X followed by c^(-1). No Noetherian, dimension or invertibility assumption on X is required.

source.place: Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2(1), with the completed coefficient convention in Section 6.5; explicit ULift and constant-scalar normalization.

proof.text: Restrict WithAbs.equiv to the integer subrings. Their membership conditions are definitionally identical; the resulting ring equivalence is isometric. Postcomposition gives an isomorphism from lifted continuous A-valued functions to continuous functions valued in lifted O, with inverse postcomposition by the inverse equivalence. Constants, operations and restriction maps are preserved pointwise. Lift the underlying ring equivalence to s:A^up≃O^up.

proof.text: The normalized finite quotient equivalence sends [x] to [x.down].up. Quotient surjectivity shows that it commutes with every adjacent transition. Apply the constant-sheaf functor and take the limit of this diagram isomorphism. Compose with the specified pbcCompletedComparison to identify B_X with the finite coefficient limit. Its composite with the completed scalar and each limit projection is the constant sheaf quotient map followed by the finite quotient equivalence, by the recorded normalization of adicDatumScalar.

proof.text: Use the normalized continuousCoefficientCompletion isomorphism and the continuous-function isomorphism of step 1 to get c:B_X≃A_X. To verify the scalar equality, cancel the limit isomorphism, test each finite projection and cancel the finite continuous-functions comparison. The constant-sheaf adjunction reduces equality to constant presheaf elements, then evaluation at a point. On the left the quotient equivalence returns the lifted residue of s(a); on the right the completion comparison returns the residue of the constant continuous function a. Their normalization formulas identify them. Extensionality for continuous functions, the constant-sheaf adjunction and limit hom-ext finish the proof.

lean.statement:
theorem continuousIntegralCoefficientComparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] :
    ∃ (s : ULift.{u + 1} (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E) ≃+* PbcIntegralRing l E)
      (c : pbcAdicCompletion X (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ≅
        latticeCoefficientSheaf X (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E)),
      (constantSheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
          s.toCommRingCatIso.hom ≫ pbcCompletedScalar X (pbcIntegralDatum l E) =
        continuousCoefficientConstantMap X (latticeCoefficientIntegers l E) ≫ c.inv
